content.title: About
content.content: Flank steak is a cut of beef taken from the abdominal muscles (the flank). It has a pronounced beefy flavor, moderate fat, and a fibrous texture. It is ideal for quick searing, marinating, and grilling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flank steak is considered a more "budget" cut, but when cooked properly it delivers great taste.
It is traditionally used in Mexican cuisine for fajitas.
The meat is rich in collagen, making it especially tender when slow‑braised.
In the United States the term "London broil" often refers to the cooking method rather than the specific cut.
Marinating flank in lime, garlic and spices enhances its flavor.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports the nervous system and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Rich in creatine and carnitine
items.content: These compounds aid energy metabolism in muscles.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may contribute to elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels can aggravate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Marinate flank steak for 2–4 hours, then sear quickly over high heat to medium‑rare and let rest 5–10 minutes. It can also be sliced thinly across the grain for fajitas or braised in a sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh flank steak in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage freeze it in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking.
